rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Einstein's mass-energy relation** E = mc² makes mass and energy two faces of one quantity, with c² = 9×10¹⁶ as the exchange rate. One atomic mass unit corresponds to **931.5 MeV**; an electron's rest energy is 0.51 MeV. Consequences: mass grows with speed (m = m₀/√(1 − v²/c²)), energy has inertia, and particle physics routinely converts mass ⇄ energy (pair creation, annihilation).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - E = mc² - 1 u = 931.5 MeV/c² → E = 931.5 MeV - m = m₀/√(1 − v²/c²)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Rest Frame: E = mc² gives energy in the object's rest frame. For moving objects: E² = (pc)² + (m₀c²)² (energy-momentum relation).  ·  Nuclear vs Chemical: Chemical reactions involve eV-scale energies (negligible mass change). Nuclear reactions involve MeV-scale energies (measurable mass defect).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Mass and energy are equivalent: E = mc²."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The Sun*** — fuses ~4 million tonnes of mass into radiation every second.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **1 u = 931.5 MeV** — the nuclear conversion constant; c must be squared.  ·  **Everyday energy changes mass immeasurably** — a year of a 100 W lamp converts 35 μg.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Mass Is Frozen Energy Einstein's 1905 insight collapsed the wall between mass and energy: E = mc². A single kilogram holds 9×10¹⁶ joules — the output of a large power plant for years. Nuclear physics is where that equivalence stops being a curiosity and becomes arithmetic.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The relation $$E = mc^2$$ - Energy and mass are equivalent and interconvertible; c = 3×10⁸ m/s is the conversion factor. - **Rest mass energy** of a particle: E₀ = m₀c². For 1 u: E = 1.66×10⁻²⁷ × (3×10⁸)² ≈ **931.5 MeV** — the key nuclear conversion. - Electron (9.1×10⁻³¹ kg): E₀ = 9.1×10⁻³¹ × 9×10¹⁶ ≈ 8.2×10⁻¹⁴ J = **0.51 MeV**.…

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Find the energy released when 0.5 g of matter is fully converted.** — E = mc² = 0.5×10⁻³ × 9×10¹⁶ = 4.5×10¹³ J.

rows.text: ### Deep dive: mass defect is the binding energy Einstein's relation $E = mc^2$ says mass is a form of energy with an enormous exchange rate: 1 kg ↔ 9×10¹⁶ J, and 1 u ↔ 931.5 MeV. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Conservation: Mass-energy is conserved, not mass and energy separately. In E = mc², mass converts to energy and vice versa.  ·  No verified PYQ; NEB-style practice (statement 2–3m, conversions 2–3m).  ·  Why did it take a nuclear age to test E = mc²?
